newsitem.title: UK: BA says cargo tonnes rise but revenue drops.
newsitem.headline: BA says cargo tonnes rise but revenue drops.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Monday it carried more cargo and increased its cargo tonnes kilometres (CTK) in the three months to end June but cargo revenue per CTK dropped.

In its detailed quarterly financial and operating statement, BA said average fuel price in the quarter was 66.92 US cents a US gallon or 4.0 percent below the 69.68 cent level in the same period last year. In the 12 months to end-March, BA's average jet fuel cost was 75.90 cents.
BA carried 197,000 tonnes of cargo in April-June, up 8.8 percent from the same period last year and compared to 721,000 tonnes in BA's fiscal year to end-March.
Cargo revenues per CTK - a standard industry measure - slipped 5.3 percent in Apr-Jun to 14.34 pence which was below the 14.78 pence achieved in the 1996/97 financial year.
